@@ -0,0 +1,209 @@ +## #4407 - Path kernel: no silent recovery from a rejected result, and the facts of its two crate edges + +Part of #4023. Review of PR #4383 (the path kernel to `main`), class B +and the minor items, review of 2026-11-27 on head `7cd322966`. A sub-PR +of `side/path-kernel`. + +### Plain summary + +- The new path planner is still off: no program changes. +- Where the new planner cannot use what it tried (an entry, a lead-out, a + geometry result), it now always says why. It either refuses with a named + reason, or it uses another way and writes a note that names the check + that failed. Before this change, some of these cases were silent. +- The converter that writes the moves of the new planner now refuses an + exit whose retract is under the clearance height. Before, it moved the + retract up to the clearance height and said nothing. + +### What was decided + +**The rule.** Never recover in silence from a refused or rejected +result. Each place refuses by a name of its own stage, or it records the +fallback with a note (or a named `Fallback`) that names the failed check. + +1. **An unoriented cutter-centre area is refused, not made normal + again** (`region_build.rs`). The builder called `Region::new` on a + centre whose loops disagreed with their nesting. Now the centre goes to + `PlanarRegion::new` as the booleans gave it, and that constructor + refuses it with `NOT_ORIENTED`. The canonical form is the contract of + `camcraft-geometry` (each region is normal), so a fault there must be + seen, not hidden. A public value still cannot reach the refusal (the + geometry gives only normal regions; K1 decision 10 of + `4025-kernel-region.md`), so the guard is pinned on the loops + themselves: `region_check::tests::a_loop_against_its_nesting_is_found`. + Dropped: keeping the re-normalisation and removing the refusal (the + constructor would then accept a centre that no check reads). +2. **A cut above the material top says why** (`entry/stage.rs`). The + tool goes straight down in air. `ABOVE` (now public) is the reason of + the named fallback where `needs_fallback` asks for one (an asked hole + or column), and the text of a note where the asked kind was not an air + entry (a helix, a ramp, a plunge, an arc lead). An asked air entry gets + neither: it is the entry flown. Dropped: a `Fallback` for an asked + entry into material, because law 4 (`needs_fallback`) says that an + entry outside material in its place is not a fallback. +3. **One checked path for the retract of an exit** (`entry/exit.rs`). + `Exit::new(lead_out, retract, top)` and `Exit::proved` call the same + `check_retract`. The check refuses a retract or a top that is not + finite, a retract under 0 (`BAD_EXIT`), and a retract under the + material top (`RAPID_IN_MATERIAL`). `Exit::new` gets the material top + as a new argument (the work of #4415, done here after #4406 merged); + its callers in the law suite and in the converter's tests pass the top + of their fixtures. The converter refuses an exit under its clearance + height as well (item 4). +4. **The converter refuses a retract under the clearance height** + (`kernel_emit/pen.rs`, `EXIT_UNDER_CLEARANCE`). It moved the retract + up to the clearance height in silence. Now `retract` returns a + refusal for a height under the clearance height (minus `EMIT_TOL`) and + for a height that is not finite. A lift retracts to the clearance + height exactly, so lifts do not change. The converter's own test plans + used an exit of 5 above the level (Z 3, under the clearance of Z 10); + they now use the clearance height (12 above the level). +5. **An exit with no lead-out names its fallback** (`entry/exit.rs`). + `Exit` has a `fallback()`: asked `arc lead-out`, used `straight + retract`, with the reason `NO_LEAD_OUT_ROOM` (no arc fits where the + tool cuts nothing), `NO_END_DIRECTION` (the last cut has no direction + at its end), or the reason of a lead refusal other than + `LEAD_OFF_ROOM`. An empty or zero-area room is "no room"; a room with + an area that `Area::new` refuses (a point that is not finite) is now a + refusal of the exit. The converter writes the fallback to the notes: + `exit: straight retract instead of the arc lead-out - `. +6. **A refused try keeps its reason** (`entry/{air,hole,column,material}.rs`, + `entry/room.rs`). Each `.ok()` and `let Ok(..) else` on a checked + constructor (`Entry::new`, `Entry::led`, `Lead::new`, `Area::new`, a + straight lead) goes through `Ctx::checked`, which keeps the kind and + the named reason. The stage still tries the next place or kind. When an + entry fits, each refused try is a note (`entry: a try of the + was refused by its check - `). When none fits, the reasons go + into the refusal: `Refusal::after` and `Refusal::tried`, and the text + form ends with `; tries refused: ...`. An empty air zone or an empty + column is "does not fit" (no note), not a refused check. A geometry + error of the room tests (`Ctx::holds`, the clip of an air lead) is now + a refusal with the kind of the error, not "does not fit"; a helix point + that is not finite is refused by name, not "does not fit". +7. **The trochoidal pitch** (`load/trochoid.rs`). The review named line + 188 as an `.ok()`; the line is the clamp of the asked pitch to the + engagement limit (the limit times the tool diameter). The clamp stays + (the limit is the user's law), and the load verdict now says it: `load: + the trochoidal pitch is limited to

mm by the engagement limit, + under the asked mm`, whenever the asked pitch is above the limit + (also when no stretch gets loops: the note says the pitch that the + stage plans with). The same search found + `load/rings.rs`: a piece of a ring level that `Curve::new` refused was + dropped. A piece too short to be a curve (`BAD_CURVE`, `ZERO_LENGTH`) + is still no ring there; each other refusal is now a refusal of the + stage. +8. **An empty arc output has its own reason** (`kernel_emit/arcs.rs`, + `ARC_EMPTY`): a circle cut whose chords are all under the tolerance + gives no arc. It was reported as `ARC_NOT_MONOTONE`. +9. **A geometry error keeps its kind.** The four `geo()` helpers + (region, guide, load rings, entry) take a `GeoError` and give + `_GEOMETRY` for `OutOfRange` and the new + `_GEOMETRY_INVALID` for `Invalid`, through one function + (`geo_refusal` in `lib.rs`). The reason is a `&'static str`, so the + text of an `Invalid` error is not carried; its kind is. +10. **The circumcentre of the medial axis** (`geometry/geo2d/medial.rs`) + checks its denominator (finite, not zero) before the division. The + result does not change: a flat or non-finite triangle gave `None` + before too. +11. **The planner switch** is read one time for each process + (`OnceLock`); its doc comment now says that a later change of the + variable has no effect until the process starts again. + +**The rest of the class (the search of the crate and of +`kernel_emit/`).** These stay, with the reason: +- The link stage (`link/approach.rs`, `link/proof.rs`, `link/route.rs`): + a chord, an approach or a room that cannot be proved (a geometry error + included) gives a lift with a named `LiftReason`. A lift is the named + fallback of the record ("Stage 5: Link") and it goes to the notes + (`LinkTally`). No change. +- `load/law.rs`: a stock reader that does not know a place + (`material_at` gives `None`) counts as material. This is the documented + contract of `StockRead` (the stage must not claim a proof); it can only + add load, never hide it. +- `unwrap_or` on an index into a list of the same length + (`order/stage.rs`, `load/rings.rs`, `load/trochoid.rs`, + `region_check.rs`), `unwrap_or_default` on the first point of a curve + that has points by construction (`guide/cover.rs`, `guide/trace.rs`), + and the first lead-out point in `pen.rs` (a lead has two or more points + by construction): no result is refused there. +- `entry/room.rs` `air_zone`: the approach distance is limited to half + the tool radius, and the limit is a note (`capped`). No change. + +**Readings.** No measured count of the kernel readings changed +(`kernel_laws` k3, k4 and k6a): see the PR body for the results. + +### `WRITE_GOLDEN=1` + +The baseline goldens of `kernel_baseline` (and the other golden suites) +are written again when a run sets `WRITE_GOLDEN`. What guards a silent +re-record: +- The gate never sets the variable (`xtask/`, `scripts/` and + `.github/` do not name it), so a gate run always compares. +- The goldens are committed files under `crates/motion/tests/golden/`. + A re-record is a diff of those files in the PR, and the review reads + it. The module doc of `kernel_baseline` says that a golden must not + move unless the output change is intended. +No new mechanism: a check that fails a run under `WRITE_GOLDEN` would +change the procedure of each golden suite of the repository, which is +outside this issue. + +### The fig8 2D Pocket readings test + +The test is in PR #4328 (`issue/3752-kernel-pocket-recipe`), which is +not merged into `side/path-kernel`. This PR does not change it. + +### Dependency facts of the two edges + +AGENTS.md **No new dependency between our crates without a decision**. +The maintainer approved the crate and its two edges on 2026-11-25 (record +of #4024 in `RECOMMENDED.md`, heading `## #4024`, "Dependency decision"). +This section gives the facts that the record left for K1, from the `use` +lines of the code on `side/path-kernel`. + +**`camcraft-pathkernel` -> `camcraft-geometry`** + +Imported items (`crates/pathkernel/src/`): +- `geo2d::{Loop, Point2, Region}` (re-exported from `lib.rs`), with the + methods of `Region` that the stages call: `new`, `empty`, `offset`, + `union`, `intersect`, `difference`, `sweep`, `contains`, `holds_path`, + `clip_polyline`, `area`, `loops`; +- `geo2d::GeoError` (`lib.rs`, the four `geo()` helpers); +- `geo2d::arc_points` (`entry/air.rs`, `entry/material.rs`); +- `geo2d::{point_segment_distance, segment_gap, segments_cross}` + (`link/proof.rs`); +- `geo2d::{RingClip, offset_side}` (`guide/rings.rs`, `guide/trace.rs`); +- `geo2d::MEDIAL_MAX_SAMPLES` and the medial axis of `Region` + (`guide/medial.rs`). + +Why the caller cannot pass them in: they are the data of each stage (the +region, its loops and points) and the operations on that data (offset, +booleans, sweeps, clips). A stage computes with them on each call; a +value or a closure from the caller would have to carry the whole polygon +engine. + +What rebuilds when `camcraft-geometry` changes: `camcraft-pathkernel` +and its tests, then each crate that depended on geometry before the edge +(`motion`, `sim`, `app`, `ui` and the others). The edge adds no new +rebuild: geometry was already under motion. + +**`camcraft-motion` -> `camcraft-pathkernel`** + +Imported items (`crates/motion/src/`, outside the tests): +- `machining2d/kernel_region.rs`: `Bounds`, `Chain`, `KernelRegion`, + `MaterialSide`, `Refusal`, `Selection`, `Stage`, `ToolShape`, + `WorkPlane`, `region`, `region::OPEN_NEEDS_SIDE`, + `region::REGION_GEOMETRY`; +- `kernel_emit/`: `entry::{Entry, Exit}`, `link::Hop`, `plan::{Cut, + Plan, Step}`, `guide::Circle`, `PlanePoint`, `WorkPlane`; +- `lib.rs`: `pub use camcraft_pathkernel as pathkernel` (the app reaches + the crate, its switch values among them, through this re-export, with + no direct edge). + +Why the caller cannot pass them in: they are the planner itself (the +stage functions and the checked types of their results). Motion calls +them; no value of motion can stand in for them. + +What rebuilds when `camcraft-pathkernel` changes: `camcraft-pathkernel`, +`camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app`, `camcraft-ui` and their tests. A +change does not rebuild `geometry`, `cl`, `gcode`, `tools`, `post`, +`sim`, `kernel` or `gpu`.
